newsitem.title: USA: Duke sees McGuire nukes down at least 3 wks. [CORRECTED 17:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Duke sees McGuire nukes down at least 3 wks. [CORRECTED 17:30 GMT]

text.p: Duke Power Co said Thursday it expects its McGuire nuclear power units 1 and 2 to be down for at least three weeks while it corrects a problem with a battery bank that serves both units.
The two units, in Cornelius, N.C., have a combined generation capacity of 2,258 megawatts (MW).
"We are estimating three weeks to a month," said company spokesman Richard Zuercher, when asked how long the two units likely would be shut.
Duke was forced to start shutting down the units after one of the facility's four battery banks failed to meet performance criteria during a recent test.
"We have (a replacement) battery bank on order," he said.
The batteries provide backup power to the McGuire facility's safety and control systems.
Zuercher said Duke did not anticipate problems meeting electricity demand from its customers. (Corrects to clarify Duke did not anticipate problems meeting demand, adding dropped word "problems")
"We're running our fossil-fuel units full out."
Duke's Oconee nuclear facility, in Seneca, S.C., is also shut following a steam pipe rupture in September that scalded seven employees, four of them critically.
The three power units at the Oconee plant produce a combined 2,538 MW of electricity.
Duke still has not set a restart date for the Oconee units, but said Wednesday it was unlikely they would be back on line before mid-November, as the company had earlier hoped.
Zuercher said nuclear generation, though only one-third of Duke's overall generation capacity, typically accounts for about two-thirds of the power it puts on the grid.
The McGuire and Oconee units together represent about 26 percent of Duke's overall 18,500 MW of generation capacity.
Duke also operates the Catawba nuclear power station at Clover, S.C., where two units each produce 1,129 MW, but only has a 25 percent ownership in Catawba unit 1.
Zuercher said Catawba 1, which trimmed power output earlier this week for minor repairs, is expected to be back at full production by Friday.
